title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook captures Redwood Inference’s standardized process for enterprise customer onboarding, ongoing support, escalation handling, integration guidance, known issues and workarounds, and recurring health checks / QBR (Quarterly Business Review) materials. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Technical Support (Tier 1–3), and partner-facing sales engineers.

Goals

- Provide a repeatable, measurable onboarding path that minimizes time-to-value for enterprise customers.
- Define clear escalation paths and SLAs to maintain customer trust.
- Surface typical integration patterns and recommended configurations.
- Centralize known issues, workarounds, and monitoring checks to accelerate resolution.
- Standardize health-check cadence and QBR content to drive upsell and reliability conversations.

Scope

This document covers hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. It does NOT replace customer-specific contractual obligations (SLA terms, compliance addenda) — those remain in Finance & Legal.

Owner and Primary Contacts

- Playbook owner: Aisha Patel (Customer Success)
- Primary escalation contact (CS Ops): Daniel Kim (eng-support)
- Technical lead (Onboarding): Riley Chen (Solutions Engineering)

Roles & Responsibilities

- Customer Success Manager (CSM): overall onboarding owner, relationship management, QBRs, feature adoption.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical onboarding lead, configuration, integration support, runbook handoff.
- Technical Support (Tier 1–3): incident handling per support process and escalation playbook.
- Eng-SRE / Runtime Team: triage for production incidents and long-term fixes.
- Account Executive (AE): commercial follow-ups and contractual questions.

Onboarding Checklist (Recommended 8–10 week plan for typical enterprise)

1) Contract & Admin (Week 0)
   - Verify signed MSA, SOW, and payment setup.
   - Provision account(s) and RBAC roles; create initial API keys (notes on rotation policy).

2) Kickoff (Week 0–1)
   - Attendees: CSM, SE, customer engineering, security contact, PM/PO.
   - Agenda: success criteria, timeline, integration type (hosted, dedicated, private), compliance requirements.
   - Deliverables: project plan, milestone dates, contact matrix.

3) Technical Intake & Network (Week 1–2)
   - Collect network topology (for Private/Dedicated): IP allowlists, VPC peering/Transit, proxy details.
   - For Private: validate on-prem hardware sizing or cloud instance types (reference sizing table below).

4) Integration & Validation (Week 2–6)
   - SE runs integration tests: auth flows, request/response validation, streaming, function calling if used.
   - Provide example SDK calls, sample prompts, and embedding index plumbing.
   - Run performance smoke tests (latency p50/p95 goals, throughput).

5) Security & Compliance (parallel)
   - Verify encryption in transit, KMS/HSM integrations, logging/audit requirements.
   - Execute any necessary security questionnaire (SSO, SCIM, SOC2 artifacts).

6) Pre-Go-Live (Week 6–8)
   - Production data migration checklist, rate limit planning, throttling behavior.
   - Final runbook handoff to customer ops and Redwood support.

7) Go-Live & Post-Go-Live (Weeks 8–12)
   - Monitor health checks for 72 hours intensive period.
   - Weekly check-ins for first 30 days; then transition to monthly health cadence.

Onboarding Deliverables (examples)

- Project plan with milestone dates
- Network configuration doc and firewall rules
- Auth keys and RBAC mapping
- Performance test report (p50/p95/p99)
- Runbooks for failover and incident response

Sizing & Reference Table (Private / On-Prem guidance)

| Workload Type | Typical Model | Minimum GPU | Expected Throughput | Notes |
|---------------|---------------|-------------:|--------------------:|-------|
| Low-latency chat | 7B / q4_k_m | 1 x A100 40GB | 15–30 rps | Good for internal pilots |
| Production chat | 13B–33B / quant | 2–4 x A100 80GB | 50–200 rps | Use batching + KV caching |
| Large-batch embeddings | 1–4B embed model | 4+ x A100 | 500–2000 qps | Prefer GPU pooling and async workers |

Escalation Playbook (Summary)

Severity definitions and target response SLAs are aligned with our support tiers in contracts.

- Sev-1 (Critical / Production down): Customer-facing service outage impacting multiple users or data loss. Target initial response: 15 minutes. Target mitigation timeline: 4 hours.
- Sev-2 (High / Degraded): Significant performance degradation (p95 latency >> SLO) or feature broken for many users. Initial response: 1 hour. Mitigation ETA: 24 hours.
- Sev-3 (Medium): Functional bug with workaround; no immediate user impact. Response within 4 business hours.
- Sev-4 (Low / Enhancement): Non-urgent requests, feature asks. Response within 2 business days.

Escalation steps (numbered)

1. Triage in Zendesk/Jira Service Management (Tier 1): capture logs, customer environment, API key, request ids, timestamps, and example payloads.
2. If logs indicate runtime error or capacity issue, escalate to Tier 2 (SE/Support Engineer) and attach profiling traces and request IDs.
3. For suspect kernel/runtime bugs or cluster-level incidents, Tier 2 escalates to Eng-SRE and Runtime team; open internal incident in PagerDuty if Sev-1.
4. For security incidents, follow Security & Compliance incident guidelines and notify Security Leads within 30 minutes.
5. Regularly update customer via Slack/email every 30–60 minutes for Sev-1, every 4 hours for Sev-2 until mitigated.

Triage Checklist (what to collect on first contact)

- Customer name, account ID, contact person and phone.
- Whether issue is reproducible and sample payload.
- Affected model, endpoint, region, and API key used.
- Request IDs, timestamps, p95/p99 latency sample, error messages, and any stack traces.
- Recent config changes or rollouts.

Support Process: Ticket Lifecycle

- Intake: Ticket created in Zendesk (or partner portal) with required triage fields.
- Acknowledgement: Auto-acknowledgement + assigned SLA.
- Triage: Tier 1 attempts resolution; if not resolved in timebox, escalate.
- Fix & Verification: Implement fix (configuration change, rollback, hotfix). Customer verifies.
- Close: Document resolution steps, root cause, and actions. Link to postmortem if Sev-1.

Integration Guides (common integration patterns)

- Hosted API: Recommend per-route timeouts (30s default), streaming for long generations, and response validation when using function calling. Include SDK snippet examples.
- Dedicated: Use client-side rate limiting + circuit breaker. Configure autoscaling policies in Redwood Dedicated console; avoid spikes > 2x sustained RPS.
- Private/VPC: Validate DNS, certificate chain, and MTU. Provide container image verification steps and image signing notes.

Known Issues & Workarounds (abridged)

| Issue | Symptoms | Workaround | Owner |
|-------|----------|-----------|-------|
| Occasional p95 latency spikes under bursty traffic | p95 latency spikes > 3x baseline | Enable autoscale burst config; reduce batching window; enable prefix KV cache | eng-sre |
| Tokenization mismatch with third-party tokenizer | Slightly different token counts leading to prompt truncation | Normalize tokenization in client; use Redwood tokenizer SDK helper | eng-serving-runtime |
| TLS handshake failures on Private deploys after OS update | Intermittent connection resets | Verify certificate chain and restart proxy; pin OpenSSL minor version if required | eng-private-deployments |

For each known issue, link to per-issue runbook (see related_pages).

Health Checks and QBR Materials

Standard health-check cadence:
- Day 0–30: Weekly 30–60 minute operational syncs.
- Month 1–3: Bi-weekly check-ins focusing on performance and adoption.
- Ongoing: Monthly health check; Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs).

Health-check checklist (monthly)

- System health: p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rate, throttling events.
- Cost metrics: tokens per successful request, average tokens per session, overall spend vs budget.
- Reliability: uptime (SLA adherence), incident summary, open bugs.
- Adoption: top features used (chat, embeddings, reranking), top consumers (routes), and retention.
- Security & Compliance: audit log status, key rotation schedule, pending compliance items.

QBR Agenda (recommended 60–90 minutes)

1. Executive summary (5–10 min): key wins, high-level usage trends.
2. Reliability & performance (15 min): incidents since last QBR, SLA status, improvements.
3. Usage & cost (15 min): tokens, spend, cost optimization suggestions.
4. Roadmap & product updates (10–15 min): relevant features and upcoming deprecations.
5. Adoption & growth opportunities (10 min): success stories, suggested pilots, expansion areas.
6. Action items & next steps (10 min): owners and dates.

QBR Deliverables

- 1-page executive summary slide
- 2–3 slides: performance and incident highlights
- Cost optimization recommendations (top 3 suggestions)
- Action tracker with owners and dates

Operational Playbooks & Attachments

- Link: Escalation playbook (internal) — see related_pages entry.
- Template: Onboarding project plan (spreadsheet template) — attach in Confluence attachments.
- Template: QBR slide deck (PPT) and 1-page exec summary (PDF).

Reporting & Dashboards

CSM and SEs should use the Redwood Console dashboards for per-route token cost, latency heatmaps, error rates, and SLO compliance. Recommended dashboards:

- Per-account latency + error rate (7d/30d)
- Token spend and cost per successful request
- Recent deploys and rollout success rate

Postmortems & Continuous Improvement

- For Sev-1 incidents, open a postmortem within 72 hours; assign RCA owner and publish in confluence/incident-review.
- Track remediation actions in JIRA and include progress in monthly health checks.

Appendix: Quick CLI & SDK snippets

- Example cURL (basic generation):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"Hello"}'

- Example Node snippet (short):
  const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });
  const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-13b', input: 'Summarize the following...' });

Document maintenance

- Owner must review this playbook every 6 months or after any Sev-1 incident.
- Update related_pages and known issues when new patterns emerge.

End of document.
